title: The Future of Work: Challenges and Opportunities for the Public Sector

title: Recoding America: Why Government Is Failing in the Digital Age and How We Can Do Better
description: Join us for a 90 minute virtual workshop with Jennifer Pahlka, former U.S. Deputy Chief Technology Officer under President Obama, founder of Code for America, and co-founder of the United States Digital Response. In her recently released book, Recoding America: Why Government Is Failing in the Digital Age and How We Can Do Better, Jennifer makes the case that government at all levels has limped into the digital age - offering online services that can feel even more cumbersome than the paperwork that preceded them and widening the gap between the policy outcomes we intend and what we get - and that government is often hamstrung by a rigid, Industrial-era culture, where policy is set from the top-down and not enough focus is placed on the details of implementation. In this workshop, Jennifer will share examples from her experiences working inside and outside of government and offer lessons learned on how we can move towards a system where we create bottom-up solutions in government, bring more people to the decision-making table, and insist on policy and process simplification to get systems that work for people in government and the residents they serve.

title: Program Evaluation Series: Understanding Program Evaluation Essentials
description: Program evaluation is a systematic process of assessing the design, implementation, and impact of a project or initiative to determine its effectiveness, efficiency, equity, and overall value. In this 90-minute virtual training, participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of how program evaluation empowers professionals in state and local governments to make informed choices, enhance program effectiveness, ensure optimal resource allocation, and take into consideration equity opportunities and challenges. Participants will learn the fundamentals of each of the six steps in program evaluation; understand the differences between inputs, outputs, and outcomes; identify sources of data and data collection; the importance of stakeholder engagement; how to communicate program evaluation results; and ethical considerations in program evaluation. Community engagement goes a step further by specifically focusing on the involvement and empowerment of local residents and community members in decisions that affect their lives, fostering inclusivity, and promoting shared ownership of initiatives. In this 90-minute virtual training, participants will learn to harness diverse perspectives through stakeholder and community engagement for comprehensive program evaluations that drive positive outcomes to help communities reach their societal goals. title: Program Evaluation Series: Crafting Logic Models and Developing Indicators
description: A logic model is a visual representation that outlines the logical connections between a program's inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes, and impacts, helping to illustrate the program's theory of change and expected results. Indicators are measurable and observable variables used to track progress and assess the achievement of specific outcomes and impacts outlined in the logic model, providing tangible evidence of a program's effectiveness. In this 90-minute virtual training, participants will develop the skills to construct robust logic models and meaningful indicators that will streamline evaluation efforts, leading to more precise insights into program effectiveness, efficiency, and equity. Participants will learn about the purposes and components of logic models; how to develop and define program inputs and activities, outputs, and outcomes; create logic model visuals; select and develop indicators; data collection methods; and ethical considerations. Real-world examples will be used to illustrate the key points in the workshop.

title: Towards Deep Listening: Rethinking Public Engagement Through Generative AI
description: Join us for this 60-minute virtual workshop with Eric Gordon, professor of Civic Media at Emerson College and director of the Engagement Lab. This training will provide a practical framework for government practitioners to rethink why and how public engagement happens at a time when most public-serving institutions are facing significant trust deficits. The availability of generative AI tools creates new opportunities for “deep listening” practices, in which public sector workers can make sense of large data sets, provide feedback in multiple languages, and for government agencies to process input with transparency and accountability. The workshop will cover these practices and will offer use cases to imagine what’s possible, as well as address potential harms that may arise with these technologies.

title: Creating a Culture of Digital Accessibility Through a Role-Based Approach
description: Join us for this 60-minute virtual workshop with Mike Gifford, Senior Strategist at CivicActions and a thought leader on digital accessibility in the public sector. Most governments, if they consider accessibility at all, will either appoint, hire or contract a subject-matter expert (SME). This workshop will explore a role-based approach, in which responsibility is distributed to everyone on the digital team, and how this role-based approach can help create culture that supports accessibility. Participants will learn about a role-based approach to accessibility, understand how responsibilities for compliance can be distributed across a digital team, and learn about existing government resources supporting a role-based approach. Participants will walk away from the workshop with an understanding of how a role-based approach makes it possible to fix barriers earlier, and create more robust, cost-effective solutions to accessibility.

title: Applying Trauma-Informed Design to Improve Government Services
description: Join us for this 90-minute virtual workshop with Rachael Dietkus, a licensed clinical social worker-designer and trauma-informed design expert currently working with the United States Digital Service and the founder of Social Workers Who Design. This workshop is designed for individuals and teams working in government and public sectors, focusing on using trauma-informed care principles to improve how services are designed, delivered, and offered. It highlights the importance of understanding trauma, especially among groups that have faced historical neglect or discrimination. The session provides essential knowledge and practical steps for applying a trauma-informed approach in designing services. The workshop will include real-life case examples that help participants learn and use six key ideas of trauma-informed care: ensuring safety, building trust, working together, empowering individuals, giving people choices, and considering cultural, historical, and gender-related matters.

title: The Art and Science of Civic Entrepreneurship
description: Join us for this 90-minute virtual training with Shannon Arvizu, Public Service Fellow in Tech & Society Group at Georgetown University and a Senior Advisor to the Chief Data Officer in the U.S. Department of Commerce. In recent years, the Biden Administration and Congress have passed a historic legislation portfolio, resulting in hundreds of new programs and projects. To administer these new changes, federal agencies and state and local governments have had to rapidly improve their strategic and operational capabilities. In this workshop, you’ll explore the ways that the public sector has evolved in recent years to better deliver the right things, in the right way, and at the right speed for the communities they serve. • Understand the capabilities of language models in generating personalized reading prompts and interactive discussion frameworks
  • Explore best practices for implementing these tools to foster engagement and improve comprehension in diverse classrooms
  • Analyze real-world applications of language models, including their strengths, limitations, and potential for enhancing literacy outcomes

description: Focus on mastering reading fluence using AI-powered tools that leverage Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) to guide read-aloud practice and provide personalized feedback. Fluency is a critical component of literacy, and ASR technology is enabling students to practice reading aloud with immediate, tailored guidance. Through hands-on experience, participants will explore ASR-driven tools for literacy instruction to support diverse learners, improve reading fluency, and foster a love of reading.

  • Explore ASR-driven tools for literacy instruction to support diverse learners, improve reading fluency, and foster a love of reading

title: Reading Challenges Revealed: AI Innovation in Dyslexia Assessments
description: Discover how AI advancements are revolutionizing dyslexia screening and support in this interactive session. Learn about the latest advancements in identifying and addressing reading challenges with precision and equity. Through hands-on demonstrations of the latest tools and expert insights, workshop participants will explore practical ways to integrate these innovations into your literacy strategies and empower diverse learner.

  • Learn about the latest advancements in identifying and addressing reading challenges with precisions and equity

  • Explore practical ways to integrate these innovations into your literacy strategies and empower diverse learners

title: Smart Literacy Instruction: Using AI and Speech Recognition to Teach Reading
description: In today’s fast-evolving digital landscape, educators are constantly seeking innovative ways to support literacy development and enhance student engagement. In this hands-on workshop, participants will explore how AI-powered applications and speech recognition software can personalize reading instruction, providing real-time feedback on pronunciation, fluency, and comprehension. They will also learn how these technologies can help students with diverse learning needs, such as English language learners, by offering tailored learning experiences and fostering independent reading practices.
short_description: Participants will explore how AI-powered applications and speech recognition software can personalize reading instruction, providing real-time feedback on pronunciation, fluency, and comprehension.

• Explore how AI-powered applications and speech recognition software can personalize reading instruction, providing real-time feedback on pronunciation, fluency, and comprehension

  • Learn how AI technologies can help students with diverse learning needs

title: Reading Together with AI: Tools for Parent-Led Learning
description: Explore how AI-powered tools can transform at-home reading support in this engaging session designed for parents, caregivers, and anyone else interested in providing reading support beyond school hours. Discover innovative technologies that make literacy development more interactive, personalized, and accessible. Through hands-on demonstrations and expert guidance, learn practical strategies to provide wraparound support that empowers readers and fosters a lifelong love of learning.

  • Learn practical strategies to provide wraparound support that empowers readers and fosters a lifelong love of learning

title: From Plans to Preparedness: Using GenAI as a Practice Partner in the Public Sector
description:
The wildfires are burning—how do we respond? Cities have plans, but are they truly prepared? In a world of rapid change and emerging challenges, public sector organizations need more than plans—they need readiness. 

This workshop introduces GenAI as a “practice partner” for governments, offering a low-cost, high-impact way to prepare for extreme weather events, misinformation campaigns, and other complex emergencies. Participants will explore how GenAI can be used to run dynamic scenario exercises, tabletop simulations, and role-playing activities that adapt in real-time. These exercises help teams build agility, improve collaboration, and strengthen their capacity to respond to the unexpected.

Drawing from real-world examples, including a recent wildfire scenario run for city managers, this session will show how GenAI can help public sector leaders practice and refine their responses, becoming more adaptive and prepared for emergent futures.
short_description: This workshop introduces GenAI as a “practice partner” for governments, offering a low-cost, high-impact way to prepare for extreme weather events, misinformation campaigns, and other complex emergencies.
learning_goals:
• Understand the role of GenAI as a “practice partner” for dynamic preparedness exercises
  • Learn how to create and run scenario-based training for city executives  and teams
  • Explore real-life applications of GenAI in disaster response and emergency planning
  • Gain practical tools for integrating GenAI into preparedness efforts to build more agile and adaptive organizations

title: Power to the Public: Making Government Work Through People-First Innovation
description:
What if government services were designed to truly meet the needs of the people they serve? This workshop, led by Tara Dawson McGuinness, co-author of Power to the Public: The Promise of Public Interest Technology, dives into a groundbreaking framework for improving public systems through a blend of technology, design, and empathy. Whether you’re grappling with challenges in healthcare, education, housing, or social services, the strategies explored in this session will equip you to deliver better, more impactful results.

Drawing on real-world case studies and practical examples, the workshop unpacks three transformative concepts:

1. Problem-Centered Thinking: Explore how understanding challenges through the lens of those affected can uncover root causes and illuminate more effective solutions. Learn how to identify and align stakeholder needs while keeping equity at the forefront.

2. Data-Driven Approaches: Discover how ethical, real-time data collection and analysis can provide actionable insights to optimize resources, reduce inefficiencies, and improve decision-making. We’ll discuss the importance of maintaining privacy, fostering transparency, and addressing potential biases in data usage.

3. Iterative Design: See how prototyping, testing, and refining solutions can lead to sustainable improvements. This process involves embracing failure as a step toward success and engaging in continuous learning to ensure long-term effectiveness.

Through an engaging mix of interactive discussions and case studies, such as improving access to social programs and creating streamlined service delivery systems, you’ll see how these principles have been successfully applied in various public sector contexts.

This workshop isn’t just about theory—it’s about action. Participants will leave with practical tools and strategies to apply these concepts in their own organizations, helping to create services that are more equitable, efficient, and responsive to the communities they serve.
short_description: This workshop, led by Tara Dawson McGuinness, co-author of Power to the Public: The Promise of Public Interest Technology, dives into a groundbreaking framework for improving public systems through a blend of technology, design, and empathy.
learning_goals:
• Understand the three foundational principles: design, data, delivery can be combined to solve public problems
  • Analyze real-world examples of how these principles have transformed public services (from ending homelessness, to rat abatement to improving uptake of benefits)
  • Address ethical challenges, including privacy concerns and equitable access to resources
  • Workshop hosted in collaboration with the Oregon Agile Community of Practice

title: Understanding, Identifying, and Addressing Administrative Burden
description: Ever felt stuck navigating complex government forms, processes, or requirements? You’re not alone. Join our Administrative Burden Workshop, hosted by the Behavioral Insights Team, to explore how unnecessary administrative hurdles create barriers to accessing essential services—and how we can fix them. This interactive session will equip you with practical strategies to identify and reduce administrative burden, making services more efficient and accessible for both the public and frontline staff. Learn how plain language, process simplifications, and other tools can transform service delivery. Whether you're a policymaker, program manager, or service designer, this workshop will give you actionable tools to streamline operations and improve user experience.
short_description: This interactive session will equip you with practical strategies to identify and reduce administrative burden, making services more efficient and accessible for both the public and frontline staff.
learning_goals:
• Identify Administrative Burden – Recognize common forms of administrative burden, such as complex forms, lengthy processes, and confusing requirements, and understand their impact on public access to essential services

  • Apply Simplification Strategies – Learn and apply key techniques, including plain language, process redesign, and behavioral insights, to reduce administrative barriers and improve service delivery

  • Implement User-Centered Solutions – Develop actionable strategies to streamline operations and enhance the user experience, benefiting both the public and frontline staff in government programs

title: Building Inclusive Climate Resilience with Human-Centered Design in Government
description:
Climate resilience work in local government is complex—it requires meaningful community engagement, inclusive decision-making, and access to the right tech, data, and resources. But what enables municipalities to do this work well? And what stands in the way, especially given shifting federal policies?

This workshop explores the intersection of Human-Centered Design (HCD), climate resilience, and civic tech—not just how local governments apply HCD principles to climate action, but also what supports or hinders their efforts in developing tech-enabled climate solutions.
short_description: This workshop explores the intersection of Human-Centered Design (HCD), climate resilience, and civic tech—not just how local governments apply HCD principles to climate action, but also what supports or hinders their efforts in developing tech-enabled climate solutions.
learning_goals:
• Understand Local Government Perspectives – Gain insights from local government staff on the opportunities and challenges of implementing climate tech resilience efforts
  • Engage Communities in Climate Solutions – Learn strategies for co-designing climate tech-enabled solutions that align with community needs and priorities
  • Navigate Implementation Challenges – Explore the key challenges of deploying tech-enabled climate resilience initiatives, including data collection and supporting community-led actions
  • Leverage Climate Data Tools – Develop skills to access and use climate data resources from local, state, and federal governments to support informed decision-making

title: Reimagining Public Institutions: Rethinking Leadership for Organizational Transformation
description:
Join Christian Bason, Ph.D., Co-founder of Transition Collective, for a 90-minute virtual training on the evolving role of leadership in driving institutional change in the public sector. As governments face increasing complexity, leaders must move beyond traditional management models to foster adaptability, collaboration, and innovation.

This session will explore how public sector leaders can create conditions for meaningful change by shifting mindsets, rethinking structures, and enabling teams to navigate uncertainty. Drawing from real-world examples, Christian will offer insights into new leadership practices that empower organizations to be more responsive, human-centered, and impactful.
short_description: Join Christian Bason, Ph.D., Co-founder of Transition Collective, for a 90-minute virtual training on the evolving role of leadership in driving institutional change in the public sector.
learning_goals:
• Lead institutional change with a future-oriented mindset
  • Balance structure with flexibility in decision-making
  • Foster a culture of trust, learning, and collaboration
  • Navigate challenges in transforming bureaucratic systems

title: Opportunities for Practical Federalism
description: In this session, participants will explore the complex interplay between federal and state governance, examine common challenges in implementing federal programs at the state level, and learn effective strategies for maximizing state autonomy while maintaining compliance with federal requirements. The workshop will cover practical topics such as federal grant management, opportunities for state policy innovation within federal frameworks, and techniques for productive engagement with federal agencies. Attendees will gain actionable insights into leveraging federal resources while preserving state interests, understanding key Supreme Court decisions affecting state authority, and identifying opportunities for policy leadership within the federal system.
short_description: In this session, participants will explore the complex interplay between federal and state governance, examine common challenges in implementing federal programs at the state level, and learn effective strategies for maximizing state autonomy while maintaining compliance with federal requirements.
learning_goals:
• Differentiate between exclusive federal powers, state powers, and shared authorities to identify opportunities for greater autonomy and policy innovation while maintaining compliance with federal requirements and achieving program objectives
  • Apply lessons from successful intergovernmental partnerships to improve collaboration with federal agencies, focusing on effective communication strategies, negotiation approaches, and relationship-building techniques

title: Del Big Data a la IA: Liderazgo para una transición digital responsable en el sector público (From Big Data to AI: Responsible Public Digital Transformation)
description:
La transformación digital en el sector público va más allá de la adopción de nuevas tecnologías: requiere liderazgo, visión estratégica y un enfoque responsable. En este taller, exploraremos el papel del liderazgo público en la transición del uso de datos masivos (Big Data) hacia la inteligencia artificial (IA), abordando oportunidades, riesgos y estrategias para una implementación ética y efectiva.

Con la experiencia de Santiago Garcés, CIO de la ciudad de Boston, conoceremos casos reales y buenas prácticas sobre cómo las administraciones pueden aprovechar el poder de los datos y la IA para mejorar la toma de decisiones, la prestación de servicios y la confianza ciudadana.
short_description: Con la experiencia de Santiago Garcés, CIO de la ciudad de Boston, conoceremos casos reales y buenas prácticas sobre cómo las administraciones pueden aprovechar el poder de los datos y la IA para mejorar la toma de decisiones, la prestación de servicios y la confianza ciudadana.
learning_goals:
• Principios clave del liderazgo en la transformación digital
  • Cómo garantizar el uso responsable de datos e IA en el sector público
  • Estrategias para impulsar la innovación sin comprometer la ética y la transparencia
  • Casos de éxito y desafíos en la implementación de IA en gobiernos locales

title: Diseño participativo de servicios públicos con apoyo de inteligencia artificial (Co-Creating Public Services with AI Assistance)
description: En esta charla se explorarán procesos y herramientas que facilitan la integración del diseño participativo en la definición de problemas y el desarrollo de soluciones innovadoras a problemas públicos con el apoyo de la inteligencia artificial. A través de este nuevo enfoque, se discutirán nuevas herramientas de participación y consideraciones clave para colaborar de manera efectiva y equitativa con diversas comunidades.
short_description: En esta charla se explorarán procesos y herramientas que facilitan la integración del diseño participativo en la definición de problemas y el desarrollo de soluciones innovadoras a problemas públicos con el apoyo de la inteligencia artificial.
learning_goals:
• Identificar los principios fundamentales del diseño participativo y su aplicación en la resolución de problemas públicos

  • Explorar herramientas y metodologías que incorporan inteligencia artificial para mejorar la participación ciudadana en la toma de decisiones

  • Analizar estrategias para fomentar una colaboración equitativa con comunidades diversas en el desarrollo de soluciones innovadoras

  • Evaluar casos de estudio donde el diseño participativo y la IA han sido utilizados con éxito en el sector público

title: Diseño de Servicios Públicos y el Uso Estratégico de la IA Generativa (Public Service Design and the Strategic Use of Generative AI)
description: Este taller explorará cómo la inteligencia artificial generativa puede potenciar el diseño de servicios públicos, abriendo oportunidades a la creación de experiencias más eficientes, personalizadas y centradas en el usuario. Además de las oportunidades, se discutirán los desafíos éticos y operativos asociados con su implementación.
short_description: Este taller explorará cómo la inteligencia artificial generativa puede potenciar el diseño de servicios públicos, abriendo oportunidades a la creación de experiencias más eficientes, personalizadas y centradas en el usuario.
learning_goals:
• Comprender los principios básicos del diseño de servicios y su relación con la inteligencia artificial generativa

  • Identificar oportunidades para mejorar la eficiencia y personalización de los servicios públicos mediante el uso de IA generativa

  • Analizar los principales desafíos éticos y operativos en la implementación de IA generativa en el sector público

  • Explorar casos de estudio y mejores prácticas en la aplicación de IA generativa en el diseño de servicios

title: Cómo Redactar una Política de IA Generativa para tu Jurisdicción (How to Write a Generative AI Policy for Your Jurisdiction)
description: A medida que la inteligencia artificial generativa se incorpora al sector público, las administraciones deben desarrollar marcos de gobernanza claros para su uso responsable y efectivo. En este seminario, exploraremos el proceso de creación de una política de IA generativa para el gobierno, tomando como referencia la experiencia de la ciudad de Boston en el desarrollo de sus directrices. Los participantes conocerán los principios clave detrás de esta política, el estado de su implementación y las decisiones estratégicas involucradas en su desarrollo. Además, se analizarán casos concretos en los que los funcionarios públicos pueden aprovechar la IA generativa para mejorar su trabajo, garantizando un enfoque alineado con la ética, la transparencia y la eficiencia gubernamental.
short_description: En este seminario, exploraremos el proceso de creación de una política de IA generativa para el gobierno, tomando como referencia la experiencia de la ciudad de Boston en el desarrollo de sus directrices.
learning_goals:
• Conocer el proceso de desarrollo de las directrices de Boston para el uso de IA generativa en el servicio público, presentado por el Director de Información de la ciudad

  • Comprender los avances y desafíos en la implementación de una política de IA generativa en la administración pública

  • Identificar escenarios específicos en los que los trabajadores del gobierno pueden utilizar la IA para mejorar su desempeño y eficiencia

  • Explorar el proceso de toma de decisiones y las recomendaciones clave para diseñar una política de IA generativa en el ámbito gubernamental

title: Innovating in the Public Interest: Getting Started
description: Just about everyone who has worked on collaboration across sectors describes the critical importance of working with the right team on a narrowly defined project with the potential to scale. We will talk about what it takes to launch a project that can be sustained and deliver outstanding performance.
short_description: Learn what it takes to launch a project that can be sustained and deliver outstanding performance.
learning_goals:
• Assess Cross-Sector Partnerships – Learn how to evaluate potential collaborations between public and private entities to ensure alignment with public-sector goals.

  • Identify Key Stakeholders – Determine who should be involved in a partnership and how to engage them effectively to support public priorities.

  • Establish a Strong Foundation – Develop strategies for launching sustainable and high-impact initiatives while maintaining public accountability.

title: Innovating in the Public Interest: Winning Early
description: Great projects begin with early wins. We will talk about the importance of driving for early wins – and of using them to build understanding of how collaborators are each evaluated and rewarded for successes.  Early successes can become the foundation for longer-term initiatives.
short_description: Participants will learning the importance of driving for early wins – and of using them to build understanding of how collaborators are each evaluated and rewarded for successes.
learning_goals:
• Design Early Wins – Learn how to structure quick, targeted successes that build trust, demonstrate impact, and reinforce public-sector credibility.

  • Navigate Cross-Sector Dynamics – Understand how different organizations measure success and leverage early achievements to strengthen long-term collaboration.

  • Overcome Skepticism – Explore strategies to gain buy-in from internal and external stakeholders by demonstrating clear public value.

title: Innovating in the Public Interest: Innovating Organizationally
description: Most of us tend to think about innovation in service delivery as the biggest opportunity for cross-sector collaboration, but many successful projects focus instead on rethinking how work is done. Technologies such as AI, data analytics, and digital platforms can enhance public service efficiency, but only when used responsibly. In this session, we will talk about how to integrate innovation in ways that improve collaboration, strengthen public-sector capabilities, and maintain transparency.
short_description: In this session, participants will learn how to use new tech to collaborate in ways that can lead to breakthrough performance.
learning_goals:
• Reimagine Public-Sector Workflows – Discover how innovation in organizational processes can enhance public-private collaborations and service delivery.

  • Leverage Emerging Technologies – Learn how tools like AI, data analytics, and digital platforms can be used responsibly to improve efficiency while ensuring equity and transparency.

  • Implement Ethical Innovation – Explore best practices for integrating new technologies in ways that uphold public trust and mission alignment.

title: Innovating in the Public Interest: Learning and Pivoting
description: Just about every cross-sector collaboration project hits a brick wall at some point. What does it take to get past that challenge while staying true to public priorities? We will talk about how strong public-private partnerships adapt, learn, and pivot while keeping long-term goals and public accountability in focus.
short_description: Participants will how to recognize the “brick wall” that almost always arises with cross-sector collaboration – and how to overcome challenges through learning and pivoting to a new agenda that reflects the priorities that you initially expose.
learning_goals:
• Anticipate and Address Roadblocks – Recognize common challenges in public-private collaborations and develop strategies to navigate them effectively.

  • Adapt to Changing Needs – Learn when and how to pivot initiatives while staying aligned with public-sector goals and community priorities.

  • Strengthen Collaborative Resilience – Develop skills to manage setbacks, rebuild momentum, and sustain cross-sector partnerships over time.

title: Innovating in the Public Interest: Growing
description: It’s counterintuitive, but many projects fail during the growth stage. Problems can arise when new stakeholders aren’t integrated effectively, when expectations outpace capacity, or when expansion moves beyond the initiative’s original public mission. In this session, we will talk about what it takes to grow responsibly while protecting the integrity of public-sector initiatives.
short_description: In this session, we will talk about what it takes to grow responsibly while protecting the integrity of public-sector initiatives.
learning_goals:
• Scale Responsibly – Learn how to expand initiatives while maintaining alignment with public values and ensuring long-term sustainability.
  • Integrate New Stakeholders – Develop strategies to onboard new partners effectively and preserve the integrity of public-sector initiatives.
  • Manage Growth Risks – Recognize when to slow down or decline expansion opportunities to prevent mission drift and resource strain.

title: Innovating in the Public Interest: Scaling
description: Achieving scaled impact can occur in many ways, including by transferring control of a successful project to a government agency, a public-sector partner, or by providing outsiders with access to tools and insights so they can replicate the approach. We will also talk about what it takes to measure impact effectively and ensure that public interest remains at the center of expansion decisions.
short_description: In this session participants will learn what it takes to measure impact effectively and ensure that public interest remains at the center of expansion decisions.
learning_goals:
• Transition Leadership Effectively – Explore when and how to hand off a successful initiative to a public-sector agency, a trusted partner, or an external entity.
  • Ensure Long-Term Public Benefit – Learn how to maintain accountability, impact, and accessibility as an initiative grows or transitions ownership.
  • Measure and Communicate Impact – Develop strategies for assessing outcomes, demonstrating public value, and ensuring transparency in scaling efforts.

title: Starting with Curiosity: A Beginner’s AI Guide for Public Servants
description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is everywhere—but what does it actually mean for your work in government? This beginner-friendly workshop is designed for public servants who are curious about AI but may also have questions, concerns, or hesitations. No technical background is required.

Together, we’ll explore what AI is (and isn’t), how it works behind the scenes, and how public servants can begin to navigate this rapidly evolving space with confidence, ethics, and purpose.
short_description: This workshop is for anyone in government—regardless of role or department—who wants a foundational understanding of AI and its implications for public service.
learning_goals:
• Learn the different terms and acronyms related to AI—ML, DL, GenAI, NLP, LLM—and what they actually mean
  • Discover how AI models “think,” make predictions, and where they can go wrong
  • Explore the difference between common fears about AI and the real risks public servants should watch for
  • Learn how to find your starting point in the AI landscape, based on your work and values

title: Lessons in Human-Centered Design in Government: The Cancer Moonshot Story
description:
In 2016, the U.S. government launched the Cancer Moonshot—a bold, national initiative to accelerate progress in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. But behind this ambitious mission was something equally revolutionary: a commitment to human-centered design.

This workshop takes you behind the scenes of the Cancer Moonshot to explore how centering empathy, listening deeply to people affected by cancer, and designing iteratively helped drive breakthroughs in one of the most complex and high-stakes areas of public health.

Participants will gain practical tools and inspiration for applying human-centered design to their own work—especially within large, bureaucratic systems. Whether you’re tackling health, housing, education, or other public challenges, this session offers a powerful reminder: even moonshots must stay grounded in the lived experiences of the people they aim to serve.
short_description: This workshop takes you behind the scenes of the Cancer Moonshot to explore how centering empathy, listening deeply to people affected by cancer, and designing iteratively helped drive breakthroughs in one of the most complex and high-stakes areas of public health.
learning_goals:
• Learn the key principles of human-centered design and how they can improve the delivery of public services
  • Understand methods for engaging users and stakeholders across diverse communities
  • Learn real-world strategies for navigating bureaucracy while staying focused on human impact

title: Making Tech Procurement Easier: A Simple Tool to Improve Government Solicitations
description:
If you’ve ever tried to read a government solicitation for new technology — or written one — you know how confusing and time-consuming it can be. Important details are often buried in long, dense documents, making it hard for vendors to even figure out if they should apply.

In this workshop, we’ll share a simple but powerful idea: adding a one-page “summary sheet” to technology solicitations. This evidence-based approach helps government teams clearly communicate what they’re looking for — and helps vendors quickly understand whether the opportunity is a good fit.
short_description: In this workshop, we’ll share a simple but powerful idea: adding a one-page “summary sheet” to technology solicitations.
learning_goals:
• Learn why many public sector tech solicitations are hard to navigate — and how that slows down innovation
  • Understand how a summary sheet can make solicitations clearer, faster to review, and easier to respond to
  • Learn what steps your team can take to start using this approach today

title: From Policy to Practice: Pennsylvania’s Pilot with ChatGPT in Government
description:
What happens when over 175 public employees—from different roles, backgrounds, and levels of experience—get the chance to test out ChatGPT at work? Pennsylvania’s statewide pilot program offers a rare, behind-the-scenes look at how generative AI can support real public sector challenges.

In this workshop, we’ll share key lessons from the Commonwealth’s ChatGPT Enterprise Pilot.

Whether you’re just curious or already experimenting with AI, this session offers practical insights on how to responsibly introduce generative AI in government — and what it takes to make it work for everyone.
short_description: In this workshop, we’ll share key lessons from the Commonwealth’s ChatGPT Enterprise Pilot.
learning_goals:
• Learn how employees across departments used ChatGPT to save time and improve their work
  • Learn the biggest benefits (and barriers) to using AI in government — from trust and accuracy to privacy and adoption
  • Learn real examples of how AI helped staff become innovation engines, bureaucracy hackers, and stronger communicators

title: Navigating Tech Governance in 2025: Policy, Procurement & AI
description:
Technology governance is no longer a niche topic—it’s central to how governments deliver services, manage risks, and earn public trust. In this timely and practical InnovateUS workshop, Cassandra Madison and Josiah Raiche will guide public servants through the five most important shifts shaping technology governance in 2025. Drawing on real-world examples and policy insights, the session will unpack how public sector organizations are rethinking procurement, AI oversight, data infrastructure, and cross-agency coordination.

Designed as a practical map for public service professionals, this workshop offers clear direction through a fast-evolving landscape—helping participants make better decisions, communicate more effectively across teams, and lead with clarity in the face of technological change.

Whether you’re setting strategy, managing digital tools, or navigating emerging technologies on the ground, this session will give you the context and confidence to move forward.
short_description: In this workshop, Cassandra Madison and Josiah Raichewill guide public sector professionals through the five most important shifts shaping technology governance in 2025.
learning_goals:
• Identify five emerging trends that are reshaping technology governance in the public sector in 2025.

  • Understand how these trends impact areas such as policy development, procurement practices, AI implementation, and digital infrastructure.

  • Engage in cross-functional conversations about responsible tech adoption and interagency collaboration.

title: Governing Through Uncertainty: Using Data, Digital Tools, and Generative AI to Strengthen Public Service
description:
In times of uncertainty, the public sector’s ability to adapt, respond, and deliver meaningful results becomes even more critical. In light of recent shifts at the federal level, this workshop explores how data, digital tools, and emerging technologies like generative AI can help public professionals navigate disruption, maintain mission focus, and strengthen trust in government.

Led by Neil Kleiman, Professor at Northeastern University and Faculty Director of InnovateUS, and Lamar Gardere, Executive Director of the Data Center, this session offers a roadmap for using technology and data not just as buzzwords—but as practical levers to improve outcomes, increase agility, and stay grounded in the needs of communities. Whether you’re a policy leader, program manager, or service designer, this session will offer inspiration and actionable strategies for doing more with what you have—and preparing for what’s next.

This workshop is for public servants at the state and local levels who are seeking tools and frameworks to build resilience and impact in the face of shifting conditions.
short_description: Led by Neil Kleiman, Professor at Northeastern University and Faculty Director of InnovateUS, and Lamar Gardere, Executive Director of the Data Center, this session offers a roadmap for using technology and data not just as buzzwords—but as practical levers to improve outcomes, increase agility, and stay grounded in the needs of communities.
learning_goals:
• Learn how data and digital tools can support more responsive and resilient public service delivery

  • Understand the potential and limits of generative AI in a public sector context—and how to evaluate tools with a critical, mission-oriented lens

  • Learn strategies for prioritizing modernization efforts and making the case for innovation amid political and fiscal uncertainty

  • Discuss real-world examples of how state and local governments are using data and AI to adapt programs, engage communities, and improve equity

title: Leading with Confidence: Helping Your Team Navigate AI in Public Service
description:
As AI tools rapidly enter the public sector landscape, public managers are being called to lead their teams through change—whether they are already experimenting with these tools or just beginning to explore their potential.

This workshop is designed for public managers who are ready to bring clarity, confidence, and a human-centered approach to the use of AI in government. Whether you’re already championing these tools and facing team hesitancy, or you’re personally unsure about where to start, this session will offer practical strategies for introducing GenAI thoughtfully, setting clear expectations, and supporting a culture of responsible innovation.

Led by Neil Kleiman, Professor at Northeastern University and Faculty Director of InnovateUS, this session will help public managers balance enthusiasm with caution, opportunity with accountability—and turn curiosity into action.
short_description: Led by Neil Kleiman, Professor at Northeastern University and Faculty Director of InnovateUS, and Lamar Gardere, Executive Director of The Data Center, this session will help public managers balance enthusiasm with caution, opportunity with accountability—and turn curiosity into action.
learning_goals:
• Learn frameworks for introducing AI in a way that aligns with public service values and team goals
  • Learn approaches for addressing hesitancy, building trust, and encouraging experimentation within teams
  • Discuss how to set guardrails, use policies, and accountability structures that support safe, responsible use of AI
  • Learn the presentation of an AI project planning tool

title: AI Prompts Unleashed: Transforming the Effectiveness and Efficiency of Your Policy Analysis, Program Evaluation, and Community Engagement
description:
Join Dr. Deborah D. Stine for a practical, hands-on webinar designed to empower state and local government staff in policy analysis, program evaluation, and related community engagement with the latest advancements in AI-driven prompts. Participants
will learn how to craft effective AI prompts tailored to their specific needs, interactive exercises to practice prompt creation, and actional strategies on integrating AI tools into their day-to-day activities. By the end of the session, attendees will be equipped to
boost their efficiency and effectiveness, ultimately leading to more impactful societal outcomes.
short_description: Join Dr. Deborah D. Stine for a practical, hands-on webinar designed to empower state and local government staff in policy analysis, program evaluation, and related community engagement with the latest advancements in AI-driven prompts.
learning_goals:
• Develop expertise in crafting tailored AI prompts that address specific state and local government policy analysis and program evaluation needs
  • Apply practical prompt creation techniques through interactive exercises designed to enhance community engagement and government service delivery
  • Implement actionable strategies for integrating AI tools into daily workflows to increase efficiency and drive more impactful societal outcomes

title: Should You Be a Public-Sector Leader?
description:
This workshop will consider the traits and skills that are often identified with leadership and give you some tools for assessing whether you would be a good public-sector leader. The workshop builds on two models of leaders: the traits model and the skills model. These models overlaps, but they provide different answers to the question, what does it take to be a leader?

Professor Seth Harris has been a public-sector leader, as Acting U.S. Secretary of Labor and Deputy U.S. Secretary of Labor, and he has taught public-sector leadership at Cornell University and in a certificate program offered by eCornell. His workshop will offer a small taste of a much larger body of work on public-sector leadership.  And he looks forward to taking your questions.
short_description: This workshop will consider the traits and skills that are often identified with leadership and give you some tools for assessing whether you would be a good public-sector leader.
learning_goals:
• Understand the traits and skills commonly associated with effective public-sector leadership through the traits model and the skills model

  • Analyze the similarities and differences between the traits model and the skills model to better understand diverse leadership pathways

  • Apply self-assessment tools to evaluate your own potential and readiness for leadership roles in the public sector

title: Working Together, Better: Using Behavioral Science to Strengthen Team Dynamics
description: When people work effectively in teams, they can get more done and feel more engaged. Fundamentally, the question of how people work with other people is a question of human behavior, and so “behavioral science” is a key lens organizations can use to understand and improve team dynamics. Join us for this workshop with Erin Britton and Jonathan Vayness, and learn simple tools that can help you better understand what makes a team strong.
short_description: Join us for this workshop with Erin Britton and Jonathan Vayness, and learn simple tools that can help you better understand what makes a team strong.
learning_goals:
• Better understand what makes a team strong, and why

  • Create lasting environments where teams can thrive

  • Consistently get the best ideas out of team members

title: AI and the Future of Public Education – A Briefing for State and Local Leaders
description: Explore how AI is influencing literacy and learning at scale. This session shares perspectives on how educational leaders can navigate implementation at the district and state levels. It will highlight strategic opportunities, governance considerations, and examples of how public education systems are responding to the evolving role of AI.
short_description: In this session, Michael Lubelfeld, superintendent of North Shore School District, will share perspectives on how educational leaders can navigate implementation at the district and state levels.
learning_goals:
• Identify key strategies for implementing AI literacy tools at district and state levels, including governance frameworks and policy considerations
  • Analyze real-world examples of how public education systems are successfully integrating AI into curriculum and administrative processes
  • Develop an actionable roadmap for educational leaders to evaluate, pilot, and scale AI learning technologies while addressing equity and access concerns

title: From Vision to Implementation: AI for Principals and School Boards
description: This session offers insights for school leaders exploring how AI can support literacy and learning across their classrooms and schools. Through examples and shared experiences, we’ll look at how principals and board members can approach AI integration, teacher support, and responsible decision-making.
short_description: This session offers insights for school leaders exploring how AI can support literacy and learning across their classrooms and schools.
learning_goals:
• Examine practical applications of AI tools to enhance literacy instruction and identify opportunities for implementation within your school's existing curriculum framework
  • Develop strategies for supporting teachers in adopting AI technologies through effective professional development, resource allocation, and creating collaborative learning communities
  • Formulate responsible AI governance policies that address ethical considerations, data privacy, and equitable access while aligning with your school's educational mission and values

title: Teaching with AI – Real Stories from the Classroom
description: Hear directly from educators using AI to support reading, writing, and critical thinking in their classrooms. This session shares practical examples and reflections from the field, showing how AI tools are being thoughtfully integrated to personalize learning, boost student engagement, and promote literacy—all while navigating real challenges and opportunities.
short_description: This session shares practical examples and reflections from the field, showing how AI tools are being thoughtfully integrated to personalize learning, boost student engagement, and promote literacy—all while navigating real challenges and opportunities.
learning_goals:
• Evaluate specific AI tools and implementation strategies that practicing educators are using to enhance reading comprehension, writing development, and critical thinking skills in K-12 classrooms
  • Analyze case examples of how teachers are personalizing learning experiences through AI, including differentiation techniques, scaffolding approaches, and assessment practices that support diverse learners
  • Identify practical solutions for common implementation challenges when integrating AI literacy tools, examining ethical considerations, technical limitations, and pedagogical best practices based on real classroom experiences

title: AI for Family Advocacy and Learning: Making Individualized Education Plans Accessible
description: Learn how generative AI can support families by translating, simplifying, and summarizing complex Individualized Education Programs (IEPs). This session showcases a new tool developed by the Burnes Center for Social Change's AI for Impact program in partnership with Innovate Public Schools. The tool helps parents better understand and engage with their child’s educational plan, making advocacy easier and more effective.
short_description: Learn how generative AI can support families by translating, simplifying, and summarizing complex Individualized Education Programs (IEPs). This session showcases a new tool developed by the Burnes Center for Social Change's AI for Impact program in partnership with Innovate Public Schools
learning_goals:
• Identify how generative AI technologies can transform complex educational documents into accessible formats for families, demonstrating the practical applications of the Burnes Center's translation and summarization tool for IEPs
  • Analyze real-world examples of how AI-assisted document simplification empowers parents to better advocate for their children's educational needs and participate more effectively in the IEP process
  • Explore implementation strategies for schools and districts to incorporate similar AI tools into their family engagement practices, with specific attention to equity, language access, and cultural responsiveness

title: Community Engagement for Public Professionals: Overview
description: Join Dr. Deborah D. Stine for an engaging introduction to a five-part series on community engagement tailored for state and local government. This first workshop provides an overview of innovative strategies to strengthen connections with communities. Attendees will learn effective communication techniques, how to leverage digital tools, and how to design inclusive outreach programs that resonate with diverse groups. Through real-world examples and interactive exercises, participants will discover ways to identify community priorities, foster active participation, and build trust with stakeholders. By the end of this session, you'll have practical strategies to enhance your community engagement efforts, resulting in improved public services and stronger civic relationships. Future workshops will delve into using interviews, focus groups, and surveys for data collection, and conclude with techniques for effectively communicating engagement results to policymakers and the public, emphasizing scientific and technical information.
short_description: Join Dr. Deborah Stine for an engaging introduction to a five-part series on community engagement tailored for state and local government. This first workshop provides an overview of innovative strategies to strengthen connections with communities.
learning_goals:
• Learn innovative strategies to strengthen connections with communities

  • Learn effective communication techniques, how to leverage digital tools, and how to design inclusive outreach programs that resonate with diverse groups

  • Discover ways to identify community priorities, foster active participation, and build trust with stakeholders

title: Community Engagement for Public Professionals: Interviews
description: This workshop on interviews is the second of a five-part series on community engagement, led by Dr. Deborah D. Stine. Building on the foundational strategies from the first workshop, participants will learn about the art and science of conducting effective interviews to equip state and local government staff with the skills needed to gather valuable insights directly from community members. Participants will learn how to design interview questions that elicit meaningful responses, select appropriate interviewees, and create an environment conducive to open dialogue. Through real-world scenarios, attendees will practice active listening techniques and learn how to analyze and interpret interview data to accurately reflect community needs and priorities. By the end of the session, participants will be prepared to use interviews as a powerful tool to enhance their community engagement efforts, ensuring that the voices of all stakeholders are heard and considered in the decision-making process. Future workshops will delve into using focus groups and surveys as well as effectively communicating engagement results and scientific and technical analysis to policymakers and the public.

Building on the foundational strategies from the first workshop, participants will learn about the art and science of conducting effective interviews to equip state and local government staff with the skills needed to gather valuable insights directly from community members.
learning_goals:
• Learn how to design interview questions that elicit meaningful responses, select appropriate interviewees, and create an environment conducive to open dialogue

  • Practice active listening techniques and learn how to analyze and interpret interview data

 

  • Use interviews as a powerful tool to enhance their community engagement efforts, ensuring that the voices of all stakeholders are heard and considered in the decision-making process

title: Community Engagement for Public Professionals: Focus Groups
description: This workshop, the third of a series on community engagement led by Dr. Deborah D. Stine, will focus on the use of focus groups to collect information from community members. Participants will learn how to capture a wide range of insights, design engaging and inclusive focus group questions, recruit a representative mix of participants, and create a comfortable environment that encourages open and honest discussion. Through interactive activities and case studies, attendees will learn techniques for managing group dynamics and synthesizing feedback. By the end of the workshop, participants will be equipped to use focus groups as a strategic tool in their community engagement efforts, enabling them to gather comprehensive and nuanced input that informs policy and program decisions. Future workshops will delve into using surveys as well as effectively communicating engagement results as well as scientific and technical information to policymakers and the public.

title: Community Engagement for Public Professionals: Surveys
description: In the fourth workshop of Dr. Deborah Stine's community engagement series, the focus will shift to the design and implementation of effective surveys, a critical tool for collecting qualitative and quantitative data on community attitudes, preferences, and needs. Participants will learn how to formulate clear and unbiased survey questions, select appropriate distribution methods, and ensure reasonable response rates. Through hands-on exercises, attendees will explore methods for analyzing survey data and translating findings into actionable insights. By the end of the workshop, participants will be well-prepared to utilize surveys as a pivotal element of their community engagement strategy, ensuring that data-driven decisions reflect the true voice of the community. The last workshop in the community enagement series will effectively communicate engagement results as well as scientific and technical information to policymakers and the public.

description: In the final session of Dr. Deborah D. Through practical exercises and real-world examples, attendees will learn how to craft compelling presentations and reports that highlight key insights and recommendations. By the end of the workshop, participants will be equipped with the skills needed to effectively communicate community engagement outcomes, fostering informed decision-making and strengthening public trust.

title: Generative AI for Public Sector Communicators: Tools, Ethics, and Best Practices
description: This workshop introduces public sector communication professionals to a range of generative AI tools, with a focus on their capabilities, limitations, and real-world applications. Participants will explore how these tools can be thoughtfully integrated into public communication workflows while upholding standards of quality, transparency, and ethics. The session will offer practical guidance on choosing the right tools, developing safeguards, and adapting workflows to take advantage of emerging capabilities. Together, we’ll explore two guiding questions: Which AI tools and features are most useful in public communications work, and what skills do professionals need to use them ethically and effectively?
short_description: In this session led by John Wihbey, participants will explore how these tools can be thoughtfully integrated into public communication workflows while upholding standards of quality, transparency, and ethics.
learning_goals:
• Understand the capabilities and limitations of leading large language models (LLMs) and generative AI tools in the context of public sector communications
  • Compare commercial AI models and evaluate how they can support ethical, effective workflows and content strategies in public-facing work
  • Apply generative AI tools to core challenges in public communications and assess methods to improve strategy, efficiency, and engagement

title: Leading Through Reform: Strategies to Engage Complex Teams
description: Leaders with a vision for advancing innovation at public sector organizations often face limited resources, competing priorities, and team members who aren't fully convinced. This workshop presents proven change management techniques from a federal executive who successfully navigated these exact challenges. The session will share how financial expertise can be leveraged to overcome resistance and guide agencies through significant operational transformation. Participants will learn practical approaches that deliver measurable results in complex government environments.
short_description: In this session led by Malena Brookshire, participants will learn how financial expertise can be leveraged to overcome resistance and guide agencies through significant operational transformation.
learning_goals:
• Learn perspective on building buy-in for change initiatives 
  • Gain techniques to reframe resistance as valuable feedback 
  • Learn methods to align budget priorities with reform objectives 
  • Gain strategies to communicate complex changes to diverse stakeholders
  • Use frameworks to measure reform success beyond traditional metrics

title: Making Digital Services Accessible- Why Inclusive Design Matters for Everyone
description: Many of us assume others experience the digital world just like we do—but that’s rarely the case. This workshop introduces the diverse ways people interact with digital services, including visual, auditory, motor, and cognitive differences. Participants will explore tools like screen readers, keyboard navigation, and browser extensions that simulate impairments and flag accessibility barriers. Through relatable examples—such as recovering from surgery, aging, or using broken devices—we’ll highlight how accessibility isn’t just for others: it’s for all of us. You’ll leave with easy, practical strategies to test and improve accessibility in your digital services—no prior experience with accessibility required. This session is ideal for web developers, designers, IT liaisons, content strategists, digital service managers, and all persons interested in building more inclusive, equitable public services.
short_description: This workshop introduces the diverse ways people interact with digital services, including visual, auditory, motor, and cognitive differences. Participants will explore tools like screen readers, keyboard navigation, and browser extensions that simulate impairments and flag accessibility barriers.
learning_goals:
• Explain why accessibility is essential for digital equity and user experience
  • Identify how different impairments affect how people navigate websites
  • Use basic tools like Funkify and WAVE to simulate and test accessibility
  • Recognize common accessibility issues and describe how they impact users
  • Apply simple techniques to make websites more inclusive for all users

title: Building Better Access: Portland’s GenAI Pilot for Smarter Permitting Appointments
description:
How can AI help public agencies improve access to services without increasing complexity for staff or residents? In this workshop, the City of Portland, Oregon will share how they piloted an AI-powered solution to streamline permitting appointment scheduling. With support from US Digital Response, the City took a human-centered approach to explore how AI could simplify access, improve accuracy, and support equitable service delivery.

City leaders will walk through the challenge they set out to address, the steps they took to develop and test their solution—including resident engagement and design sprints—and the results and lessons that emerged. They will also discuss how they partnered with external collaborators like US Digital Response to co-develop a practical, resident-focused tool. The session will include a demonstration of the pilot tool and space for discussion with participants exploring similar ideas in their own agencies.

This session is ideal for public servants exploring the responsible use of AI in resident-facing services, and for anyone looking to move from pilot to impact.
short_description: In this workshop, the City of Portland, Oregon will share how they piloted an AI-powered solution to streamline permitting appointment scheduling.
learning_goals:
• Describe a real-world example of how generative AI can be applied to improve a permitting process
  • Identify human-centered design principles used in AI implementation
  • Recognize common challenges and lessons learned in piloting AI in a public sector context
  • Reflect on how similar approaches might be applied in their own agencies or departments

title: AI Regulation Across Borders: Who’s Setting the Rules—and Why It Matters
description: What does it mean to “regulate” artificial intelligence? And who gets to decide how to do that? Around the world, governments and international organizations are taking different approaches to shaping the future of AI—some focused on technological advancement, others on human rights, safety, or geopolitical competition. You’ll gain a clear picture of key actors, the goals driving their efforts, and the tradeoffs each approach entails. Whether you’re working in technology, policy, or public service, this workshop will help you build foundational knowledge to engage with the fast-evolving regulatory landscape.
short_description: Around the world, governments and international organizations are taking different approaches to shaping the future of AI—some focused on technological advancement, others on human rights, safety, or geopolitical competition. You’ll gain a clear picture of key actors, the goals driving their efforts, and the tradeoffs each approach entails.
learning_goals:
• Describe the main goals and rationales behind efforts to regulate AI
  • Identify key national and international actors involved in AI governance
  • Compare different regulatory approaches between countries and across regions
  • Understand how regulatory decisions may affect public sector work and public services

title: Chatbots in Public Service: Responsible Design and Use
description: Chatbots—text- or voice-based systems that simulate human conversation—are increasingly used to provide public information, automate services, and streamline communication. But along with their promise come real challenges, from accessibility issues, to deceptive design, to data privacy and transparency concerns. In this session, we’ll unpack how conversational bots work, what they can (and can’t) do, and what risks to watch for when deploying them in the public sector. Whether you’re exploring chatbot use for your team or just want to understand the basics, this workshop will give you a solid foundation for making informed, ethical decisions.
short_description: In this session, we’ll unpack how conversational bots work, what they can (and can’t) do, and what risks to watch for when deploying them in the public sector.
learning_goals:
• Explain how text- and voice-based chatbots function and are commonly used
  • Identify public sector use cases where chatbots can be useful
  • Recognize key risks and limitations associated with conversational AI tools
  • Apply basic guidelines for responsible chatbot adoption and oversight

title: Making Homelessness Rare and Brief: Lessons from the Built for Zero Backbone Strategy
description:
Built for Zero is a national initiative demonstrating that coordinated systems change can dramatically reduce—and ultimately end—homelessness. Central to this work is a powerful intermediary model that enables backbone organizations, often state and local agencies, to align strategies, data, and resources toward population-level outcomes.

In this workshop, Melanie Lewis Dickerson, Director of Large-Scale Change at Community Solutions, will share lessons from the Built for Zero approach, focusing on how public sector professionals can play a pivotal role in supporting and sustaining local systems change. Participants will gain insight into the enabling conditions, policy levers, and organizational functions that help drive progress toward making homelessness rare and brief.
short_description: In this workshop, Melanie Lewis Dickerson, Director of Large-Scale Change at Community Solutions, will share lessons from the Built for Zero approach, focusing on how public sector professionals can play a pivotal role in supporting and sustaining local systems change.
learning_goals:
• Understand Built for Zero as a national improvement initiative working with over 150 communities to end homelessness
  • Explore the role and responsibilities of state and local backbone organizations in driving systemic change
  • Identify enabling policies and practical considerations for adopting and implementing the intermediary model

title: How to Ensure Successful AI Adoption: Making Vendors Accountable and Trustworthy
description:
With the rapid growth of AI tools marketed to the public sector, government teams face a critical question: how can we adopt new technologies while ensuring transparency, safety, and accountability? This workshop offers a practical guide to navigating the vendor landscape, evaluating AI tools, and setting clear expectations for trustworthy implementation.

This session is ideal for procurement teams, public technology leaders, innovation officers, and program managers evaluating or adopting AI tools. It is also open to any public sector professional who wants to better understand how to responsibly engage with AI vendors and support trustworthy adoption in their agency or community
short_description: This workshop offers a practical guide to navigating the vendor landscape, evaluating AI tools, and setting clear expectations for trustworthy implementation.
learning_goals:
• Learn about the growing number of AI companies offering services to government, and how to engage with them effectively—whether through procurement, pilot programs, or shared service models across agencies.

  • Explore real-world case studies and documentation protocols that clarify how AI systems work, the assumptions and choices behind them, and the questions public servants should ask to assess risk, fairness, and alignment with public values.

  • Gain tools and strategies to surface potential risks before deployment and set standards that promote ethical, safe, and effective use of AI technologies in government settings.

title: Designing AI with Humans in Mind: Insights on Inclusion, Productivity, and Strategy
description:
As artificial intelligence becomes more integrated into government operations, public sector leaders face critical questions about how this technology impacts their teams. In this interactive session, Josh Martin, former Chief Data Officer for the State of Indiana, and Jamie Kimes, founder of The Idea Garden, will explore how AI can be a force for good—especially when it comes to supporting neurodiverse individuals and unlocking new forms of human potential. The conversation will also address a rising tension in many agencies: while productivity is increasing with AI, so is anxiety among employees. Participants will gain tools to recognize these dynamics and shape long-term strategies that prioritize inclusion, trust, and team well-being.

This workshop is designed for public sector professionals working in technology, human resources, organizational development, and leadership roles—and for anyone interested in creating more inclusive, people-centered strategies for AI integration.
short_description: In this interactive session, Josh Martin, former Chief Data Officer for the State of Indiana, and Jamie Kimes, founder of The Idea Garden, will explore how AI can be a force for good—especially when it comes to supporting neurodiverse individuals and unlocking new forms of human potential.
learning_goals:
• Identify ways AI can support neurodiverse talent in public sector work environments.

  • Understand the emerging phenomenon of “productivity anxiety” and its organizational implications.

  • Evaluate the human impact of AI adoption within their own teams or agencies.

  • Apply key principles to design human-centered AI strategies that are ethical, inclusive, and future-oriented.

title: AI in Action: Use Cases and Capabilities in Law Enforcement
description: What can AI actually do for law enforcement today? This session will explore the current landscape of AI applications in policing. Drawing on case studies from multiple jurisdictions, the workshop will highlight real-world implementations, core technologies like computer vision and speech recognition, and the operational opportunities and constraints public safety leaders should be aware of.
short_description: This session will explore the current landscape of AI applications in policing.
learning_goals:

  • Learn real-world implementations, core technologies like computer vision and speech recognition, and the operational opportunities and constraints public safety leaders should be aware of

title: AI Fundamentals for Public Safety
description: This foundational session will introduce law enforcement and public safety professionals to the core concepts of Artificial Intelligence, with a focus on applications in policing. Participants will learn to distinguish between generative AI, machine learning, and predictive analytics, and explore how these technologies work in practice in a law enforcement and public safety context. Designed as an accessible entry point, the workshop will clarify key terminology and functions, and lay the groundwork for understanding more advanced and policy-oriented sessions later in the series.

learning_goals:

  • Explore how AI technologies work in practice in a law enforcement and public safety context

title: AI Policy Development
description: Organizations implementing AI capabilities must have clear, well-structured policies that describe how AI is used and what safeguards are in place to ensure ethical application. Policies should be specific to each use case and serve as training and communication tools for internal teams and external stakeholders. This session will guide public safety executives through key steps in developing effective AI policies tailored to their agency’s mission.

learning_goals:

  • Understand the key steps in developing effective AI policies tailored to their agency’s mission

title: Stakeholder Engagement in AI Implementation
description: Successful AI implementation in law enforcement requires active involvement from a broad set of stakeholders, including internal departments, oversight bodies, and community representatives. This session will help executives develop stakeholder engagement strategies and processes that support trust, transparency, and shared ownership throughout the AI lifecycle—from problem definition to deployment.

  • Understand the stakeholder engagement process from problem definition to deployment

title: BIAS: Understanding and Undermining its Operation in Humans and in the Technology We Create
description: Body-worn cameras represent one of the largest investments in public safety in a generation—yet their full potential as a tool to improve police performance remains underutilized. This workshop shows how policing professionals can use body cam footage to improve officer communication and training, assess the impact of training, and even predict moments of escalation during police interactions. The session will highlight the need for multi-stakeholder collaboration to responsibly harness this rich source of data and enhance police-community relations.
short_description: This workshop shows how policing professionals can use body cam footage to improve officer communication and training, assess the impact of training, and even predict moments of escalation during police interactions.
learning_goals:

  • Understand the need for multi-stakeholder collaboration to responsibly harness this rich source of data and enhance police-community relations

title: Predictive Policing and Algorithmic Bias
description: Predictive policing tools use data to forecast potential criminal activity, but without careful oversight, these systems can reinforce existing biases and inequities. This workshop will examine how predictive algorithms are developed and deployed in law enforcement, the risks of feedback loops and discriminatory outcomes, and practical steps agencies can take to evaluate and mitigate bias. Participants will leave with strategies for using data responsibly and equitably in operational decision-making.
short_description: This workshop will examine how predictive algorithms are developed and deployed in law enforcement, the risks of feedback loops and discriminatory outcomes, and practical steps agencies can take to evaluate and mitigate bias.

  • Learn strategies for using data responsibly and equitably in operational decision-making

title: Facial Recognition: Applications, Risks, and Limits
description: Facial recognition is one of the most controversial AI tools in public safety. This session will explore how law enforcement agencies are using facial recognition, from suspect identification to surveillance, and examine the ethical, legal, and technical challenges it raises. Case examples and recent regulatory trends will inform a discussion on safeguards, accuracy, consent, and oversight. Participants will gain a deeper understanding of where facial recognition can be effective—and where its limits must be clearly defined.

title: AI-Assisted Writing: Lessons from the Field
description: An exploration of how generative AI tools can support message drafting, from speeches to FAQs—what works, what doesn’t, and how to stay in control.
short_description: Explore how generative AI tools can support message creation—from speeches and public statements to FAQs and internal communications.
